title: The Benchmark Trap: Structures of Power and Injustice in AI Evaluations
abstract: arXiv:2608.15326v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) benchmarks are not neutral tools of evaluation but socio-technical artefacts that shape competition, power, and research priorities within AI. Benchmarks standardise the assessment of systems and facilitate the creation of leaderboards that reward state-of-the-art performance with prestige, citations, trust, and institutional influence. As the costs of developing competitive AI systems rise, these rewards increasingly concentrate among powerful, industry-funded labs. This paper situates these concerns within Iris Marion Young's theories of oppression and structural injustice. It argues that current benchmarking practices may perpetuate systematic harms affecting various actors in AI research, aligning with four of Young's "faces of oppression". Benchmarking culture is further framed as a source of structural injustice, as these harms emerge from normalised, individually defensible practices and network effect

translated_title: 基准陷阱：人工智能评估中的权力与不公结构
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.15326v1 公告类型：新 摘要：人工智能（AI）基准并非中立的评估工具，而是塑造AI领域竞争、权力和研究优先级的社会技术产物。基准标准化了系统评估，并促进了排行榜的创建，这些排行榜以声望、引用、信任和机构影响力奖励最先进的性能。随着开发竞争性AI系统的成本上升，这些奖励日益集中在强大的行业资助实验室手中。本文将这些担忧置于艾里斯·玛丽昂·杨的压迫与结构性不公理论之中，认为当前的基准实践可能延续系统性伤害，影响AI研究中的各类参与者，与杨的“压迫四面孔”中的四个相符。基准文化进一步被框定为结构性不公的源头，因为这些伤害源于常态化、个体上可辩护的实践和网络效应。
tldr: 本文揭示AI基准评估并非中立，而是加剧了权力集中和结构性不公，通过奖励机制使行业巨头获益并系统性地边缘化其他参与者。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that AI benchmarks are not neutral but exacerbate power concentration and structural injustice, benefiting industry giants through reward mechanisms while systematically marginalizing other participants.
